n: David’s cry of abandonment became the words Jesus spoke on the cross. By quoting the first line, Jesus may have pointed to the whole psalm, which ends in triumph. Feeling forsaken, the sufferer still says “my God.”

f.w: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?

n: He cries day and night, yet hears no answer and finds no rest.
Still he affirms that God is holy, enthroned on Israel’s praises. Faith holds even in silence.

f.g: God is pictured as seated on a throne made of his people’s praise.

n: Israel’s ancestors trusted God, and he rescued them.
They cried to him and were saved; they trusted and were not disappointed. Why, then, is he left alone?
He feels like a worm, not even a man — scorned and despised by everyone. Isaiah describes the Messiah in similar terms.
Everyone who sees him mocks him, sneering and shaking their heads — exactly what onlookers did at the crucifixion.

f.g: Sneer, curl the lip in contempt.

n: They taunt, “He trusted the Lord — let the Lord rescue him!” The chief priests used nearly these words at the cross.

f.w: He trusted on the LORD that he would deliver him

n: Yet God brought him safely from the womb and made him trust while still nursing.

f.g: You made me feel safe, gave me trust.

n: From birth he has been cast on God’s care; God has been his God from his mother’s womb.

f.w: I was cast upon thee from the womb

n: “Don’t be far from me, for trouble is near and no one else will help.”
His enemies surround him like huge, strong bulls from Bashan.

f.g: Bashan, east of the Jordan, was famous for well-fed, powerful cattle.

n: They open their mouths at him like roaring, ravenous lions.
His strength drains away like spilled water; his bones are out of joint; his heart melts like wax — vivid images of physical agony.

f.w: all my bones are out of joint
f.g: An apt description of the strain of crucifixion.

n: His strength is dry as a broken piece of pottery; his tongue sticks to his mouth with thirst. God has laid him in the dust of death.

f.w: my tongue cleaveth to my jaws

f.g: A fragment of broken, baked clay.

n: A pack of evildoers circles him like dogs; they pierce his hands and his feet — strikingly fulfilled in the crucifixion of Jesus.

f.w: they pierced my hands and my feet
f.g: Most ancient translations read “pierced”; the standard Hebrew text reads “like a lion,” and scholars debate the original.
In that culture, scavenging street dogs — a term for outsiders and enemies.

n: He can count all his bones, and people stare and gloat over him.

f.w: I may tell all my bones
f.g: Tell = count; his bones are visible, stretched and exposed.

f.w: they look and stare upon me

n: They divide his clothes among them and cast lots for his garment — fulfilled when soldiers gambled for Jesus’s robe.

f.w: They part my garments among them

n: “But you, Lord, don’t be far away! My strength, hurry to help me!”
Rescue my life from the sword, my one precious life from the dogs.

f.g: My only one — my precious, irreplaceable life.

n: Save me from the lion’s mouth and the wild oxen’s horns — and here the psalm turns: “You have answered me!”

f.g: In Hebrew, the verse suddenly ends with “you have answered me,” marking the turn from lament to praise.

n: Now praise: “I will declare your name to my brothers; in the congregation I will praise you.” Hebrews applies this to the risen Christ.

f.w: I will declare thy name unto my brethren

n: All who revere the Lord, all of Jacob’s and Israel’s descendants — praise and honor him!

f.w: Ye that fear the LORD, praise him

n: For he did not despise the suffering of the afflicted one or hide his face; when he cried, God heard. The sufferer was not abandoned after all.

f.w: neither hath he hid his face from him

n: He will praise God in the great assembly and fulfill his vows before the faithful.

f.g: Offer the thanksgiving sacrifices promised in a time of need.

n: The humble will eat and be satisfied — perhaps a thanksgiving feast. Those who seek the Lord will praise him, and live forever.

f.w: The meek shall eat and be satisfied
your heart shall live for ever

n: All the ends of the earth will remember and turn to the Lord; all the families of the nations will worship him.

f.w: All the ends of the world shall remember and turn unto the LORD

n: For kingship belongs to the Lord, and he rules over the nations.
Rich and poor, living and dying — all will bow before him. No one can keep himself alive; all depend on God.

f.w: all they that go down to the dust shall bow before him

n: Future generations will serve him and will be told about the Lord.
They will proclaim his righteousness to people not yet born: “He has done it!” Some hear in this an echo of Jesus’s final cry, “It is finished.”
